questions.question: BD and CE are the medians of Δ ABC, right angled at A. If CE = frac{{5sqrt {13} }}{2} cm, BC = 10 cm, then the length of BD is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

BD and CE are the medians of Δ ABC

CE = 5√13/2 cm

BC = 10 cm

**Concept used:**

When two median is given, then add the two numbers in the middle and then divide by 2.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edb53fbe5497401ebeeb640a1c2227121465f95e52c4973a866eeaa6287c0cff.png] 

According to the question

⇒ BD² = AB² + (AC/2)²

⇒ BD² = AB² + AC²/4

Now,

CE² = (AB/2)² + AC²

⇒ AB²/4 + AC²

Now,

BD² + CE² = 5/4(AB² + AC²)

⇒ BD² + CE² = 5/4 BC²

⇒ BD² + (5√13/2)² = 5/4 × (10)²

⇒ BD² + 325/4 = 5/4 × 100

⇒ BD² + 325/4 = 125

⇒ BD² = (125 – 325/4)

⇒ BD² = (500 – 325)/4

⇒ BD² = 175/4

⇒ BD = 5√7/2 cm

**∴ The length of the BD is 5√7/2 cm**

questions.question: A can complete a certain work in 30 days. He started the work. After 4 days, B joined him and the whole work was completed in 10 days from the beginning. B alone can complete one-third of the same work in:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 30 days

Time taken by B to complete the work after 4 days = 10 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let B can complete the work in x days

Time taken by A to complete the work in 1 day = 1/30 units

Time taken by B to complete the work in 1 day = 1/x units

According to the question

⇒ 10 × 1/30 + (10 – 4) × 1/x = 1

⇒ 1/3 + 6/x = 1

⇒ 6/x = (1 – 1/3)

⇒ 6/x = 2/3

⇒ 2x = 18

⇒ x = 9

B alone can complete one-third of the same work = (1/3 × 9)

⇒ 3 days

**∴ The required time is 3 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

According to the question, A can complete a work in 30 days, 

After 4 days of work B join and completed the remaining work next 6 days, 

What A alone can do in 26 days that work A + B can do in 6 days, so

⇒ A × 26 = (A + B) × 6

⇒ 26A = 6A + 6B

⇒ A/B = 6/20 = 3/10

So, total work is 30 × 3 = 90 unit

Now, B can do 1/3ᵣd of the work in 90 × 1/3 × 1/10 = 3 days

(224 – 1)

⇒ (2³)⁸ – 1

Now,

⇒ (1 – 1)/7

questions.question: As observed from the top of a lighthouse, 42 m high above sea-level, the angle of depression of a ship sailing directly towards it changes from 30° to 45°. The distance travelled by the ship during the period of observation is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the angle of elevation (or depression) of a tower of height h changes from θ₁ to θ₂ as an object moves directly towards it, the distance travelled is:

Distance = h × (cot θ₁ − cot θ₂)

Here, h = 42 m, θ₁ = 30°, θ₂ = 45°

Distance = 42 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Distance = 42 × (√3 − 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e7eb57492f4e8ed7e1520931e65b2310f3a7ad59fb5b406a3d3d4ea60fbae88.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the lighthouse (AB) = 42 m

Angle of depression at initial position C = 30° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ACB = 30°

Angle of depression at final position D = 45° ⇒ Angle of elevation ∠ADB = 45°

**Formula Used:**

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

In right-angled triangle ΔABD,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 = 42 ÷ BD

⇒ BD = 42 m

In right-angled triangle ΔABC,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 42 ÷ BC

⇒ BC = 42√3 m

The distance travelled by the ship is CD, which is the difference between BC and BD.

⇒ Distance CD = BC − BD

⇒ Distance CD = 42√3 − 42

⇒ Distance CD = 42(√3 − 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 42(√3 − 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heights and Distances (Trigonometry)

The angle of elevation is the angle formed between the horizontal reference line and the line of sight when looking up at an object. The angle of depression is the angle formed when looking down from a height.

Two Objects on the Same Side

If two objects are observed on the ground from a tower of height h at angles θ₁ and θ₂, the distance separating them is easily calculated as h(cot θ₁ − cot θ₂).

Two Objects on Opposite Sides

When two objects are situated on opposite sides of a central tower of height h, having respective angles of elevation θ₁ and θ₂, the total distance between them is h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂).

questions.question: If a + b + c = 7 and a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = 301, then ab + bc + ca = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relationship: (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) = (a + b + c) × [(a + b + c)² − 3(ab + bc + ca)]

Substitute the given values: 301 = 7 × [7² − 3(ab + bc + ca)]

⇒ 301 ÷ 7 = 49 − 3(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 43 = 49 − 3(ab + bc + ca)

⇒ 3(ab + bc + ca) = 6 ⇒ ab + bc + ca = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of variables (a + b + c) = 7

Sum of cubes (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) = 301

**Formula Used:**

1. a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − (ab + bc + ca))

2. (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f147d029c8d5ef82d9c500b3471e060ca638438c9f86d1d8529b0dc0356abfaf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let ab + bc + ca = x

⇒ From identity (1): 301 = 7 × (a² + b² + c² − x)

⇒ a² + b² + c² − x = 43 ⇒ a² + b² + c² = 43 + x

⇒ From identity (2): (7)² = (a² + b² + c²) + 2x

⇒ 49 = (43 + x) + 2x

⇒ 49 = 43 + 3x

⇒ 3x = 49 − 43

⇒ 3x = 6

⇒ x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Special Case: a + b + c = 0

If the sum of variables is zero, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Alternative Form of Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 1/2(a + b + c)[(a − b)² + (b − c)² + (c − a)²].

Square of Trinomial

The expression (a + b + c)² always equals a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca).</p

questions.question: By selling 3 dozen oranges for Rs. 405, a trader loses 25%. How many oranges should he sell for Rs. 288 if he needs to earn a profit of 20% in the transaction?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

SP of 3 dozens oranges = Rs. 405

Loss = 25%

**Concept used:**

3 dozen = 36 oranges [1 dozen = 12 oranges]

**Calculation:**

According to the question

SP of 36 oranges = Rs. 405

Cost price of 36 oranges = Rs. (405/75 × 100)

⇒ Rs. 540

Now,

He needs to earn a profit of 20% in the transaction = Rs. (540 × 120/100)

⇒ Rs. 648

Now,

Oranges should he sell for Rs. 288 is

⇒ (36/648 × 288)

⇒ (288/18)

⇒ 16

**∴ The required oranges is 16**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

**Concept used:**

 (N₁ times P₁)/(Rs₁) = (N₂ times P₂)/(Rs₂) 

N₁ = 36 , P₁ = 75, Rs₁ = 405 and N2 = ?, P2 = 120, Rs2 = 288

**Calculation:**

⇒ (36 times 75)/(405) = (N₂ times 120)/(288) 

⇒ N₂ = 16

questions.question: What is the cost (in Rs.) of levelling a triangular park with sides 60 m, 112 m and 164 m at the rate of Rs. 10.50 per m² ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The sides of a triangular park = 60m, 112m and 164m

The rate of levelling a triangular park = Rs. 10.50 m²

**Formula used:**

S = (a + b + c)/2

By Heron's formula 

Area of triangle = √s(s – a)(s – b)(s – c)

**Calculation:**

As we know,

S = (a + b + c)/2

⇒ (60 + 112 + 164)/2

⇒ 336/2

⇒ 168 m

Now,

Area of triangle = √s(s – a)(s – b)(s – c)

⇒ √168(168 – 60)(168 – 112)(168 – 164)

⇒ √168 × 108 × 56 × 4)

⇒ √(2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 × 2 × 2)

⇒ (2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 × 3 × 3)

⇒ 2016 m²

Now,

The cost of levelling of 1 m² of the park = 10.50 

The cost of levelling of 2016 m² of the park = (10.50 × 2016)

⇒ Rs. 21,168

**∴ The required cost is Rs. 21,168**

questions.question: If the difference between the compound interest compounded annually and the simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% per annum is Rs. 279, then the sum (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate = 10%

Time = 3 years

The difference between the CI and SI = Rs. 279

**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

CI = A – P

**Calculation:**

Let Principal be x

SI = (x × 10 × 3)/100

⇒ 3x/10

Now,

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ x(1 + 10/100)³

⇒ [x(100 + 10)/100]³

⇒ [x(110/100)³]

⇒ (x × 11/10 × 11/10 × 11/10)

⇒ 1331x/1000

Now,

CI = A – P

⇒ CI = (1331x/1000 – x)

⇒ (1331x – 1000x)/1000

⇒ 331x/1000

The difference between the CI and SI = Rs. 279

⇒ 331x/1000 – 3x/10 = 279

⇒ (331x – 300x)/1000 = 279

⇒ 31x/1000 = 279

⇒ x = (9 × 1000)

⇒ Rs. 9000

**∴ The required sum is Rs. 9000 **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

**Formula used:**

(P× r² × (300 + r))/(100³ ) = Difference between C.I & S.I for 3 years

**Calculation:**

⇒ (P× 10² × (300 + 10))/(100³ ) = 279

⇒ P = (279 × 100³)/(100 × 310)

⇒ P = 9000

questions.question: The average of 19 numbers is 48. The average of the first 7 numbers is 50.6 and that of the last 13 numbers is 47.6. If the 7th number is excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 19 numbers = 48

The average of the first 7 numbers = 50.6

The average of last 13 numbers = 47.6

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

The average of 19 numbers = (19 × 48) = 912

The average of the first 7 numbers = (7 × 50.6) = 354.2

The average of last 13 numbers = (13 × 47.6) = 618.8

Now,

7th number = (618.8 + 354.2 – 912)

⇒ (973 – 912)

⇒ 61

Sum of remaining 18 numbers = (912 – 61) = 851

The average of the remaining numbers = (851/18)

⇒ 47.3

**∴ The required average is 47.3**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Let a₁, a₂......a₁₉ are the number

⇒ a₁ + a₂ + ...a₁₉ = (19 × 48) = 912 ----(1)

⇒ a1 + a2 + ...a₇ = (7 × 50.6) = 354.2 ----(2)

⇒ a₇ + a₈ + ...a₁₉ = (13 × 47.6) = 618.8 ----(3)

Adding equation (2) and (3)

⇒ a₁ + a₂ + ..a₇ + a₇ + .....a₁₉ = 354.2 + 618.8 = 973

⇒ a₇ + a₁ + a₂ + .....a19 = 973

⇒ a₇ + 912= 973 [From (1)]

⇒ a7 = 61

Hecne new sum = 912 - 61 = 851

**∴ New average = 851/18 = 47.3**

questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs. 480. A person buys it at two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. He sells it at a profit of 25%. What is his profit (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The marked price of an article = Rs. 480

The two successive discounts = 15% and 10% 

Profit = 25%

**Here A person first buys and then sell so when he buys a goods is called his cost price and company's selling price **

So CP for person CP = MP × (100 - Successive Discount%)/100

Now he sells this on profit of 25%

So SP for person SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

**Formula used:**

CP = MP × (100 - Successive Discount%)/100

⇒ CP = Rs. (480 × 85/100 × 90/100)

⇒ Rs. (3,672,000/10,000)

⇒ **CP = Rs. 367.2**

SP = Rs. (367.2 × 125/100)

⇒ Rs. (367.2 × 5/4)

⇒** SP = Rs. 459**

**Calculation:**

For the person CP = Rs. 367.2, SP = Rs. 459

Profit = SP - CP

Profit = Rs. (459 - 367.2) 

⇒ Rs. 91.8

∴ The required profit is Rs. 91.8

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, chord AB and diameter CD intersect each other at point E, inside the circle. If ∠AOD = 42° and ∠BOC = 104°, then what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠AED?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle between two chords intersecting inside a circle is half the sum of the central angles of the intercepted arcs.

⇒ ∠AED = (∠AOD + ∠BOC) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AED = (42° + 104°) ÷ 2

⇒ ∠AED = 146° ÷ 2 = 73°

**∴ The correct answer is 73°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠AOD = 42°

∠BOC = 104°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us construct a line segment joining points A and C.

⇒ According to the Inscribed Angle Theorem, the angle subtended by an arc at the circumference is exactly half of the angle subtended by it at the centre.

⇒ For arc AD, ∠ACD = ∠AOD ÷ 2

⇒ ∠ACD = 42° ÷ 2 = 21°

⇒ For arc BC, ∠BAC = ∠BOC ÷ 2

⇒ ∠BAC = 104° ÷ 2 = 52°

⇒ In ΔACE, the exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ The exterior angle at E along the line CD is ∠AED.

⇒ ∠AED = ∠ACD + ∠BAC

⇒ ∠AED = 21° + 52° = 73°

**∴ The correct answer is 73°.**

Interior Intersecting Chords Theorem

When two chords intersect inside a circle, the angle formed between them is half the sum of the central angles subtended by the intercepted arcs. 
 Formula: ∠Interior = (Arc₁ + Arc₂) ÷ 2

Exterior Intersecting Secants Theorem

When two secants intersect outside a circle, the angle formed is half the difference of the central angles subtended by the intercepted arcs. 
 Formula: ∠Exterior = (Major Arc − Minor Arc) ÷ 2

Inscribed Angle Theorem

An angle inscribed in a circle is exactly half the measure of the central angle that subtends the same arc. 
 Formula: ∠Inscribed = ∠Central ÷ 2

questions.question: There are three numbers. If the ratio of the first to the second number is 2 : 7 and that of the second to the third number is 5 : 8, then the ratio of the first to the third number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the first to the second number = 2 : 7

The ratio of the second to the third number = 5 : 8

**Calculation:**

The ratio of the first to the second number = (2 : 7) × 5

⇒ 10 : 35

The ratio of the second to the third number = (5 : 8) × 7

⇒ 35 : 56

The ratio of the first to the second to the third number = 10 : 35 : 56

Now,

The ratio of the first to the third number = (10 : 56)

⇒ 5 : 28

**∴ The required ratio is 5 : 28**

questions.question: X and Y start at the same time to ride from place A to place B, which is 80 km away from A. X travels 4 km per hour slower than Y. Y reaches place B and at once turns back, meeting X, 16 km from place B. Y's speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

X and Y start at the same time to ride from place A to place B, which is 80 km away from A

X travels 4 km per hour slower than Y

Y reaches place B and at once turns back meeting X, 16 km from place B.

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of X be p km/hr

The speed of Y = (p + 4) km/hr

Distance travelled by Y = (80 + 16) = 96 km/hr

Distance travelled by X = (80 – 16) = 64 km/hr

According to the question

⇒ 96/(p + 4) = 64/p

⇒ 96p = 64p + 256

⇒ 32p = 256

⇒ p = 8 km

Now,

The speed of Y is (p + 4) = (8 + 4)

⇒ 12 km/hr

**∴ The required speed of Y is 12**

questions.question: In a constituency, 55% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 40% of the males are illiterate and 40% of the females are literate, then by what percentage is the number of illiterate females more than that of the illiterate males (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number of voters are males = 55%

Number of males who are illiterate = 40%

Number of females who are literate = 40%

**Calculation:**

The number of voters are males = 55%

Number of voters who are females = (100 – 55)% = 45%

Number of males who are illiterate = (55 × 40/100)

⇒ 22
